hypothesis_statement.content: The paper proposes a first comprehensive study of excitonic and polaronic physics in Ba3MA3 antiperovskite derivatives.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: In this work, we present the first comprehensive study of excitonic and polaronic physics in antiperovskite derivatives Ba3MA3 (M = P, As, Sb, Bi; A = Cl, Br, I).

evidence_result.content: Mg3NF3 has been experimentally synthesized at high temperature in a cubic structure.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Experimentally, Mg3NF3 has been synthesized at high temperatures (1050 ◦C) and adopts a cubic Pm¯3m struc- ture [14].

evidence_result.content: PBE lattice parameters agree with previous studies.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The PBE-calculated lattice parameters (Ta- ble I) agree with previous studies [12, 15, 37].

evidence_result.content: Phonon dispersion, decomposition enthalpies, and elastic constants confirm structural, thermodynamic, and mechanical stability.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Structural stability is confirmed by phonon dispersion [20] (Fig. S1), as well as decomposi- tion enthalpies and elastic constants, indicating thermo- dynamic and mechanical stability (see Secs. IV and V of the SM [25]).

evidence_result.content: PBE lattice parameters match prior studies
evidence_result.evidence_span: The PBE-calculated lattice parameters (Ta- ble I) agree with previous studies [12, 15, 37].

evidence_result.content: Phonons, decomposition enthalpies, and elastic constants confirm stability
evidence_result.evidence_span: Structural stability is confirmed by phonon dispersion [20] (Fig. S1), as well as decomposi- tion enthalpies and elastic constants, indicating thermo- dynamic and mechanical stability

evidence_result.content: All compounds are direct-bandgap semiconductors with VBM and CBM at Γ
evidence_result.evidence_span: Fig- ures S5 and Fig. 2(a–d) show that all systems are direct- bandgap semiconductors with both VBM and CBM at the Γ point.

evidence_result.content: HSE06 band gaps for Ba3MBr3 agree with earlier reports
evidence_result.evidence_span: The HSE06 band gaps of Ba3MBr3 (M = P, As, Sb) agree with earlier reports [12].

evidence_result.content: G0W0@PBE+SOC band gaps are 1.23-2.17 eV, comparable to lead halide perovskites
evidence_result.evidence_span: The result- ing G0W0@PBE+SOC band gaps (Eg) range from 1.23 2 to 2.17 eV, comparable to lead halide perovskites (1.50– 1.85 eV) [42, 43]

evidence_result.content: Effective masses indicate predominantly p-type transport
evidence_result.evidence_span: The calculated electron and hole effective masses (m∗ e, m∗ h; Table I) fur- ther indicate predominantly p-type transport behavior

evidence_result.content: Optical band gaps of 0.97-1.81 eV fall in the optimal solar-conversion range
evidence_result.evidence_span: The resulting optical band gaps (0.97–1.81 eV) lie within the optimal range for efficient solar energy conversion.

evidence_result.content: Exciton binding energies decrease from Cl to Br to I and are 0.254-0.352 eV
evidence_result.evidence_span: Table II sum- marizes the calculated EB values, which decrease from Cl- to Br- to I-based compounds and lie in the range 0.254–0.352 eV.

evidence_result.content: Exciton radii are larger than the lattice constants, indicating intermediate-radius excitons spanning multiple unit cells.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The calculated exciton radii (0.90– 1.95 nm) exceed the lattice constants (∼6–7 Å), indicat- ing intermediate-radius excitons extending over multiple unit cells and lying between Frenkel and Wannier–Mott limits [52, 53].

evidence_result.content: Phonon screening only slightly lowers exciton binding energies by 1.82–2.91%, giving modified values of 0.247–0.342 eV.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Using Eq. (1), we find that phonon screening reduces the exciton binding energy by only 1.82–2.91%, yield- ing modified values (E′ B) between 0.247 and 0.342 eV (see Table II).

evidence_result.content: Calculated Fröhlich coupling constants of 2.16–4.01 place these materials in the intermediate coupling regime.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Ta- ble III display the calculated values lying in the range, 2.16–4.01, which place these materials in the intermedi- ate coupling regime.

evidence_result.content: Bound excitons are more stable than charge-separated polaronic states in all compounds.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Table III also shows a comparison of the resulting quasiparticle gaps with exciton binding energies, con- firming that bound excitons are energetically more stable than charge-separated polaronic states in all compounds.

evidence_result.content: Highest calculated mobilities are 25.71 cm2V−1s−1 for electrons and 75.09 cm2V−1s−1 for holes.
evidence_result.evidence_span: The highest calculated mobilities are found to be 25.71 cm2V−1s−1 for electrons and 75.09 cm2V−1s−1 for holes (see Table III),

evidence_result.content: All compounds have allowed dipole transitions at Γ
evidence_result.evidence_span: As shown in Figs. 2 and S5, all compounds display allowed dipole transitions at the Γ point.

evidence_result.content: SLME increases with absorber thickness and then saturates
evidence_result.evidence_span: Figure 3 shows the thickness-dependent SLME, com- puted using the BSE@G0W0@PBE+SOC approach. It increases with thickness before saturating.

evidence_result.content: SLME improves from chloride to bromide to iodide compounds
evidence_result.evidence_span: A clear trend is observed, with SLME rising from Cl- to Br- to I-based compounds

evidence_result.content: Maximum SLME values span 19.10% to 32.41%
evidence_result.evidence_span: The maximum SLME values range from 19.10% to 32.41%.

evidence_result.content: Some compounds exceed the SLME of conventional lead-based perovskites
evidence_result.evidence_span: Notably, Ba3AsI3, Ba3SbI3, and Ba3BiA3 (A = Cl, Br, I) exhibit SLME values exceed- ing those of conventional lead-based perovskites, such as CsPbI3 (20.67% [67]) and MAPbI3 (28.97% [43]).

evidence_result.content: The studied compounds are stable direct-gap semiconductors with suitable band gaps
evidence_result.evidence_span: Our results establish these compounds as dynamically, thermodynamically, and mechanically sta- ble direct-gap semiconductors with bandgaps spanning the optimal range for photovoltaic and optoelectronic ap- plications.

evidence_result.content: Many-body calculations show moderate exciton binding and intermediate-radius excitons
evidence_result.evidence_span: Explicit many-body perturbation theory cal- culations reveal moderate exciton binding energies and intermediate-radius excitons

evidence_result.content: Carrier-phonon coupling lies in the intermediate regime
evidence_result.evidence_span: Carrier-phonon coupling is found to be in the inter- mediate regime

evidence_result.content: SLME calculations predict efficiencies up to 32%, surpassing several lead-based perovskites
evidence_result.evidence_span: Import- antly, spectroscopic limited maximum efficiency calcula- tions predict power conversion efficiencies of up to 32%, exceeding those of several state-of-the-art lead-based per- ovskites.

constraint.content: Fully self-consistent G0W0@PBE+SOC calculations are computationally too demanding for the large systems considered and the required convergence settings.
evidence_spans: Fully self-consistent G0W0@PBE+SOC calculations are com- putationally very demanding for the considered systems (relatively large unit cell size) and convergence settings.

constraint.content: For SLME evaluation, VBM-to-CBM optical transitions must be allowed, since even direct-gap materials can have dipole-forbidden transitions due to inversion symmetry and identical band parities.
evidence_spans: Before computing SLME, we examined whether optical transi- tions from the VBM to the CBM are allowed, as direct bandgap materials may still exhibit forbidden transitions due to inversion symmetry and identical band parities
